questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Composition Patterns”?
options: Composition Patterns helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Composition Patterns means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Composition Patterns removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Composition Patterns should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Composition Patterns helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Composition Patterns is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Smart and presentational patterns” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Smart and presentational patterns” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Smart and presentational patterns” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Smart and presentational patterns” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Smart and presentational patterns” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Smart and presentational patterns” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Smart and presentational patterns” under Composition Patterns. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Composition Patterns”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
